question: In its report on cohesion policy 2014-2020, the Committee on Regional Development mentions an interesting measure: specifically, this concerns the creation of a mechanism for the early detection of red tape and actions in breach of or not effectively applying the multi-level governance principle. 1.
What is the Commission’s position on this initiative?
What specific form could this mechanism take?
Above all, what changes would it mean in comparison with existing procedures?
answer: While the report tabled by the Committee on Regional Development and adopted in Plenary on 14 March 2024 does not refer to a specific mechanism for early detection of red tape as referred by the Honourable Member, it underlines simplification as one of the key drivers of the future Cohesion Policy and identifies several avenues for future simplification, including in public procurement procedures, State aid rules, use of simplified cost options and the single audit principle among others.

The report also calls on Member States to avoid over-regulation in order to ensure legal certainty for beneficiaries. The 2021-2027 Cohesion Policy regulations introduce some 80 simplification measures compared to the 2014-2020 period.

Furthermore, the ongoing discussions on the future of Cohesion Policy also identify simplification as one of the main focus areas for development of the Policy — a view that the Commission shares. The Commission also supports specifically efforts oriented towards the early detection and reduction of red tape.

In this regard, during its audits the Commission systematically reviews the presence of any rules, processes and procedures that constitute excessive administrative burden and cost or that can be simplified without undermining the overall assurance and effectiveness of the management and control system.
